name: Libration Mere
description: Libration Mere wobbles gently on its axis in a slow librational dance, causing its ocean tides to shift in complex, never-quite-repeating patterns. The result is a world where coastlines are theoretical concepts, the water advancing and retreating in irregular pulses that reshape the kelp forest shelves on a weekly basis. Submerged mountain chains rise to within meters of the surface before sinking again as the tidal patterns shift.

The air above the ocean carries a clean, briny freshness that expedition members consistently describe as invigorating. The sky is a deep cerulean, reflected perfectly in the still waters between tidal surges. When the tides shift, the silence breaks into the roar of water moving across continental shelves, a sound that can be heard from orbit during the most extreme oscillations.

The kelp forests of Libration Mere are the densest marine botanical ecosystems ever documented, their fronds reaching over two hundred meters from the seabed to the surface. These forests have adapted to the unpredictable tides by developing flexible, almost muscular stipes that bend with the current rather than breaking. The biomass produced by a single square kilometer of this kelp exceeds that of entire terrestrial forests on other worlds.

Libration Mere has been designated a botanical research priority, with three orbital stations dedicated to studying its unique marine flora. The kelp produces compounds that show promise in radiation shielding applications, attracting military interest alongside scientific. Harvesting operations must contend with the unpredictable tides, which have claimed several automated collection platforms.
